transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maeve (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood CSM), Lena (CharterPoint Head MLOps), Raj (CTO), Marta (Procurement), Devon (Infra)

Summary: Short renewal / expansion check-in. CharterPoint wants to extend contract 12 months, add EU region and explore Private/VPC option for EU data residency; also discuss dedicated capacity bump for Q1 traffic, and run a performance bench. Action items and pilot timeline agreed in principle.

Topics: capacity uplift, EU private pilot, security controls (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), pricing structure, benchmark plan, legal/PO timeline

[00:00] Maeve: hey everyone, thanks for joining. for context, quick agenda — pricing update, eu pilot, perf baseline, and next steps. hope that works?
[00:18] Lena: sounds good, thanks Maeve. we have raj and marta on for procurement questions too.
[00:25] Raj: yeah were eager to lock a 12 month extension but need the eu residency guarantee. current contract ends feb, so want onboarding in jan.
[00:38] Maeve: great — that aligns with what we discussed last week. quick clarifying q: are you planning to move sensitive traffic to Private (VPC/on-prem) immediately or a staged approach?
[00:49] Lena: staged. dev and non-PII will stay on hosted, sensitive will go to EU private. timeline: pilot in january, then ramp feb-mar.
[01:05] Omar: perfect. from a tech side we want to propose a two-phase: 1) Dedicated capacity in EU-hosted region with pinning for predictability, 2) private VPC pilot for strict residency and KMS control. that gives you fallbacks while we validate latency.
[01:23] Devon: couple of infra constraints — our on-prem team prefers HSM-backed keys; can Redwood integrate with our KMS/H-S-M?
[01:33] Maeve: yes, Redwood supports KMS and HSM integrations — note in docs as K-N-S integration sometimes in auto transcripts, heh. we'll include the specific integration pattern.
[01:43] Marta: procurement will need SOC2 attestation, iso stuff, and audit logs for model calls. do you have a SOC2 + audit log retention option for EU?
[01:55] Noah: we do — SOC2 Type II, and per-account audit logs. retention can be configured; we'll include options and cost.
[02:10] Lena: perfect. on perf — what's the expected latency delta between hosted and private? we can't exceed 200ms median for inference in our customer flows.
[02:22] Omar: depends on model and batching. with our continuous batching and KV cache (kay-vee cache) warm, we typically hit 80-150ms on Dedictaed pools EU-west for 1k token prompts. mis-transcribed earlier as Redwood Dedictaed in some notes. the private on-prem path will add network overhead but we can co-locate to meet 120-200ms depending on rack placement.
[02:47] Raj: okay so as long as we see numbers during bench. can you run our prompt set?
[02:53] Omar: yes — please share sample prompts and expected percentiles. we'll run both hosted-eu and dedicated-eu and a private-onprem sim.
[03:05] Lena: i'll upload a redacted prompt set and a small traffic profile. also note we have bursts around month end, about 2.5x baseline.
[03:16] Maeve: we can propose burst capacity in the quote — a burst pool or autoscale policy. for pricing, are you targeting the same spend or trying to reduce unit cost?
[03:27] Raj: need to reduce unit cost by 10-15% overall, but will accept slightly higher fixed reserve if it gets predictable monthly spend.
[03:36] Maeve: ok we can present two SKUs: 1) reserved capacity + lower per-token rate, 2) flexible reserved with burst credits. we'll show math.
[03:46] Marta: legal will want a fallback if Dedictaed pool has outages — automatic failover to hosted with data controls?
[03:55] Omar: yep we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies. we can set policy to route sensitive requests only to private/dedicated; non-sensitive can go hosted. in failover we can degrade to model variant with same privacy settings.
[04:12] Speaker 1: quick q — how do prefix caches behave across failover?
[04:16] Omar: prefix/K-V cache is per-runtime. if you failover to a different runtime you'll miss cache warmness for a period; we can mitigate with pre-warming strategies and KV-state replication for certain workloads.
[04:30] Lena: would that add to cost?
[04:33] Omar: some engineering cost for replication; we can include that as an opt-in.
[04:40] [-- 10 minute jump in transcript to bench planning --]
[14:45] Maeve: we need to lock dates for the bench — Omar, what's your earliest to run a 48hr perf window?
[14:52] Omar: i have a slot the week of dec 6th. need the prompt set and a small key for test tokens and vpn creds for private sim.
[15:02] Lena: we'll aim to provide by nov 29.
[15:06] Raj: procurement note: if price break is tied to commitment, we'll sign a 12 month with a 30% reserved commit for q1 and then revisit for q2.
[15:16] Maeve: that should be fine; we'll model commit tiers.
[15:21] Marta: any concerns around data exfil or logging to US jurisdictions? we need assurance logs + keys stay in eu for private flows.
[15:31] Noor? (transcription noise)
[15:34] Noah: we'll provide a data residency diagram and the private control plane topology. logs for private flow can be stored in customer-controlled S3 in eu. for hosted we maintain logs but can configure retention and region.
[15:48] Lena: good. also wanted to ask about model updates — we need pinning of model versions during the pilot; can't have model drift.
[15:58] Omar: yep model pinning and rollout policies are supported — can do canary, A/B. we'll propose an automatic fallback to last known-good model on any regression.
[16:10] Raj: competitors question — AetherAI promised on-prem connectors earlier; are there any known limits with your HSM integrations?
[16:21] Omar: no major limits; we have customers using AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure, and specialized HSMs. there could be some ops integration work. we'll detail the runbook.
[16:34] Speaker 1: (mumbles) will there be extra charges for audit logs?
[16:38] Maeve: yes configurable — base audit logs included, extended retention or SIEM forwarding is add-on. we'll show both.
[16:47] [--- pricing review/pilot mechanics discussion ---]
[25:10] Maeve: high level ask from Redwood: we want to propose a 12 month extension with a 30% reserved commit for Q1, eu dedicated pool sizing at 2 GPU nodes initially (we'll map to your qps), and option to spin private VPC pilot in eu for 90 days. is that aligned?
[25:28] Raj: yes, thats reasonable as long as costs hit our target.
[25:33] Marta: procurement will need the SOW and any amendment language for data residency. we prefer to have that by nov 30 to get vendors queued for dec sign-off.
[25:45] Maeve: we can do that; legal template + SOW by nov 26.
[25:51] Omar: we'll attach a perf runbook and the bench results within 3 business days of the run finishing.
[26:00] Lena: on monitoring — can we get token-level cost visibility by route and by model?
[26:06] Noah: yes that's in the console — token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and trace links. we'll include a short demo clip in the follow-up email.
[26:17] Devon: any special networking requirements for private pilot?
[26:21] Omar: just a peering/VPN and a small egress rule set; we'll send a network requirements doc.
[26:28] Lena: great. can we also get a demo of failure scenarios — like rapid fallback to hosted — to reassure ops?
[26:36] Maeve: yes we can script a failover demo during the pilot kickoff.
[26:40] [--- wrap-up and recaps ---]
[35:12] Maeve: quick recap: 1) Redwood to share updated 12mo pricing and SOW by 2026-11-26; 2) CharterPoint to provide redacted prompt set by 2026-11-29; 3) Omar runs perf window week of 2026-12-06; 4) pilot kickoff targeted week of 2027-01-11; 5) Marta to confirm legal approvers by 2026-11-30.
[35:37] Marta: noted. procurement will also need vendor security questionnaire answers.
[35:41] Maeve: will include security pack link: https://redwood.app/security/CharterPoint_SecPack_v1
[35:48] Raj: fine. one more small ask — can you include price per 1k tokens for embeddings separately?
[35:55] Maeve: yes, well break out embeddings vs gen rates.
[35:58] Speaker 1: thanks all.
[36:02] Omar: thanks, we'll follow up with the bench plan and share access instructions.
[36:08] Lena: thanks, look forward to the bench results.
[36:12] [crosstalk]  Maeve: ok end.

Notes on transcription: small sections have speaker mislabels and some words auto-mis-transcribed (e.g., "Dedictaed" for Dedicated, "K-N-S" for KMS, "kay-vee cache" for KV cache). Links and doc names provided are placeholders and will be updated in follow-up.

Attachments referenced: https://redwood.app/pricing/CP_proposal_v3 , https://redwood.app/security/CharterPoint_SecPack_v1
